## Description

Encodes the geometry as a base-32 GeoHash string with `precision` characters.
Non-point geometries are encoded using the center of their bounding box.
A non-positive precision
returns an empty string, and precision is capped at 20 characters.

A GeoHash is defined against the WGS84 datum, so the argument must carry either
a WGS84 CRS (`EPSG:4326` / `OGC:CRS84`) or no CRS at all; anything else raises
an error. Use `ST_Transform()` to reproject first. This includes other
geographic CRSes such as NAD83, whose units are degrees but whose datum differs
from WGS84 by enough to shift the result at high precision.

The same rule applies whether the CRS belongs to the column or to the
individual rows; only the timing differs. A column-level CRS is known while the
query is planned, so it is rejected before any row is read. A row-level CRS is
not known until the row is reached, so it is rejected then. To encode only the
WGS84 rows of a mixed column, filter them first — `WHERE ST_SRID(geom) = 4326`
is applied before the encoding, so the other rows never reach it.

Latitudes outside -90 to 90 return `NULL`. Longitudes outside -180 to 180 are
wrapped back into range when the argument declares a WGS84 CRS, so a longitude
of 181 encodes as -179; without a declared CRS they return `NULL` instead,
matching Apache Sedona.

When `precision` is omitted, the argument must be a `POINT` and is encoded at
the maximum precision of 20 characters. Any other geometry type raises an
error, because there is no single obvious precision for a geometry that covers
an area.

Geography arguments are bounded on the sphere and require the s2geography
bounder to be registered on the session.

## Examples

```sql
SELECT ST_GeoHash(ST_GeomFromWKT('POINT (21.4234 52.0423)'), 10);
```

```sql
SELECT ST_GeoHash(ST_GeomFromWKT('POLYGON ((0 0, 2 0, 2 2, 0 2, 0 0))'), 8);
```

```sql
SELECT ST_GeoHash(ST_GeomFromWKT('POINT (21.4234 52.0423)'));
```
